title: Pointed etale neighbourhood category
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] ($\Omega$ an algebraically closed field, $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ its spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum]). The category $\mathcal N_{\bar s}$ of *pointed etale neighbourhoods* of $\bar s$ has as objects the pairs $(V,\bar v)$ where $V\to S$ is an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] (an object of the small etale site $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]) and $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ is a morphism of schemes over $S$, i.e. $(V\to S)\circ\bar v=\bar s$. A morphism $(V,\bar v)\to(W,\bar w)$ is a morphism $h:V\to W$ over $S$ with $h\circ\bar v=\bar w$; composition and identities are those of morphisms of schemes. Its opposite category $\mathcal N_{\bar s}^{\mathrm{op}}$ is the index category of the stalk colimits.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
Let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point. Define
$\mathcal N_{\bar s}$ to have objects pairs $(V,\bar v)$ with $V\to S$
etale and $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ above $\bar s$.
A morphism $(V,\bar v)\to(W,\bar w)$ is an $S$-map $V\to W$ carrying
$\bar v$ to $\bar w$. We index stalk colimits by
$\mathcal N_{\bar s}^{\mathrm{op}}$ so that restriction maps point forward.

split_report.summary: Definition split: every notion now cites its node (scheme def-pc-scheme, geometric point def-weil-geometric-point, Spec def-weil-affine-spectrum, etale morphism def-weil-etale-morphism, small etale site def-weil-pbc-etale-site); the statement names the morphisms (S-morphisms carrying the chosen point, h∘v=w) and the composition, as the master blueprint sketch does; the vague reference to def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions is replaced by the specific nodes. The category is exactly Mathlib's category of elements of the fibre functor of the etale point, (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.pointSmallEtale s).fiber.Elements (read in Elements.lean:48,64-65 and EtalePoint.lean:62-64), so the item is a Mathlib leaf. The claims about it are not in the definition: that N_s is cofiltered is the existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered (which cites this item, so it is not cited back), that the affine neighbourhoods are cofinal is lemma-weil-pbc-affine-neighbourhood-cofinal, and the stalk as colimit over N_s^op is def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks (Point.presheafFiber, colimit over fiber.Elementsᵒᵖ); the last sentence of the statement only names the index category. slopmaster2 has the sorry-free abbreviation AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.Nbhd (SplitNeighborhood.lean:54-55) for the same category.
